In Hong's eyes, every problem in this world has a solution—it just takes time.
Like water dripping through stone, drop by drop, one day it will carve a hole.
The Mohist Gate's plan to conquer the skies is no different.
Hopeless for a century, measured in millennia, there lies a glimmer of hope.
He grasped this truth after barely a year in the outer sect.
Everything was predestined; he could see decades of his future in a single glance.
Delving into the mechanics of flying Yuan machines was fascinating, yet the deeper he studied, the more a century seemed to pass in the blink of an eye.
Write a few books, craft some new contraptions. Earn a title in the end, take on two or three Disciples.
Those Disciples might one day walk the path he envisioned.
He often spoke of water wearing away stone and the value of fleeting moments. The logic was sound, yet he felt something was missing... passion.
He could see the future, but he didn’t know how to persist toward it.
Should every falling droplet share the same faint glimmer?
Suddenly, he realized the world’s problems shouldn’t have just one answer.
Even if everyone’s End Point is the same, the journey there is theirs to choose.
The ancients said, "Read ten thousand books, walk ten thousand miles." He’d read the books—the miles still lay ahead.
Now, he would take that step.
